pairs.subject: agent-runtime-assembly
pairs.evidence: src/components/modules/game-systems/AIBehaviorView/index.tsx:109 When a CLI agent run ends without reporting and the server cannot grade it, every dispatched scenario is closed with the failure-class status 'error'. The 'outcome unknown' fact survives only in a free-text lastRunOutput string, because ScenarioStatus has no indeterminate member, so a reader cannot tell an unknown outcome from a real test error.

techniques.evidence: src/components/modules/game-systems/AIBehaviorView/index.tsx:110 An agent run whose outcome nobody knows is closed as 'error'. The unknown outcome is written into a message string instead of an indeterminate status, and the vocabulary (draft/ready/running/passed/failed/error) has none. Separately, runRef is an in-memory ref, so a page reload mid-run leaves rows 'running' with nothing to close them.

src/components/modules/game-systems/AIBehaviorView/index.tsx:117 The view starts sibling CLI sessions under their own session keys. No agent run launches another run here, so the re-rooting precondition does not hold.

pairs.registryProposal: indeterminate-closure-on-interruption is phrased around a restart that finds outstanding work. The same failure mode, closing an unknown outcome as a failure with the reason in a string, also occurs on the normal completion path of callback-driven task systems when a run exits without its report. The use_when triggers could name that case.
